answer: Churn is counted in thread, and reef publishes the ratio each epoch. At most 7% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. Anyone who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the saffron history. Every extra alias adds 3 hours of verification and 13 percent more locked value. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
